defects.description: RenderBatch formats every row with fmt.Sprintf inside the refresh loop, so each render of the representative batch pays the formatter's per-row heap allocations for lines that a plain byte-builder and strconv.AppendInt produce byte-identically.

trigger.expected: functional output preserved: the rendered lines stay byte-identical to the fixture's; with the rendering rewritten to a simpler builder/strconv strategy the measured allocs/op and B/op are lower than the fixture's, while the ns/op timings are descriptive only and assert no threshold
trigger.actual:

cpu: AMD Ryzen 7 5700

defects.why_missed: The suite asserts only rendered text — exact lines, batch order, empty batches — which the format-based and the builder rendering both satisfy byte for byte, and it records no allocation metric, so churn behind identical output stays invisible to a green suite.
